revision: Native GLB skin, five attached anatomical studies, long blonde hair, surface-conforming mint selections
reviewers: FORM integration agent: actual rendered poses, camera views, mobile layouts and sampled unpaused playback; this is an authored self-review, not independent clinical or artistic certification.

scope.method: Reviewed actual browser screenshots and enlarged contact sheets: six authored poses and nine view/pose combinations per study, seven unpaused samples across a loop boundary per study, and mobile rest/peak for all five studies. Also inspected rear Back-selection/clear captures. Automated checks independently compare posed body vertices, bone matrices, shared identity, exact loop endpoints, reverse seeking, surface anchors, interactions and layout.
scope.finalMaterialReview: Final selected-region tint and Back-only hair fade were checked in refreshed browser pose/view/mobile captures. The preceding unpaused playback samples use identical geometry and motion; the last change affects selection materials only.

globalRepairs: All five studies now instantiate the same optimized licensed skinned mesh instead of primitive body parts.
Kept native finger, wrist, elbow, shoulder, hip, knee, ankle and toe relationships.
Mint overlays copy the skinning/morph surface, feather their boundaries and use a garment-aware offset.
Labels use anchors evaluated on the posed surface; picking uses a cached posed body mesh.
The two-pass Loop hair refinement preserves UV seams, card connectivity, morph deltas and normalized skin weights.

repairsAndChecks: Replaced primitive assemblies with the shared CC0 skinned adult-female character.
Preserved Pectoralis, Back and Pelvis as surface selections, including posed barycentric anchors.
Added explicit Back-only hair fade and exact material/shadow restoration on clearing.
studies.observations: One clothed adult female identity occupies the full-body study. Neck, shoulders, torso, hips and legs are continuous; the reaching arm and head counter-turn are visible while both feet stay planted. Front, profile and three-quarter views retain the same proportions. The Back selection reveals the upper-back mint surface through faded hair; clearing it restores the opaque hair.

repairsAndChecks: Uses the same continuous body mesh and anatomical arm chain.
Raised sleeve-crossing surface overlays to 1.7 mm so they render above the 1.2 mm garment shell.
studies.observations: The forearm rises through a clear elbow bend while the wrist and fingers stay attached. The shoulder flows into the upper arm without a separate sphere. Sleeve-crossing overlays remain smooth after increasing their offset above the suit. Close framing intentionally shows the connected torso; in mobile arm framing its adjacent head passes beneath the fixed title.

repairsAndChecks: Uses the connected palm and finger topology from the licensed full-body mesh.
Authored staggered MCP/PIP/DIP curls and thumb opposition on native finger bones.
Preserved the hand presentation pose and independent digit selections.
studies.observations: The pinky emerges from the ulnar palm with a shorter proportion than its neighbors. All five digits remain attached through open, intermediate and curled poses; the finger chains bend at distinct joints and the thumb opposes across the palm. The front study isolates the requested hand; manual three-quarter rotation can bring the adjacent face behind the fixed title.

repairsAndChecks: Shares one leg, hip and foot surface with the full character.
Maintains support by solving pelvis translation against the forefoot during the bend.
Raised thigh overlays above the suit to remove visible depth conflicts.
studies.observations: Hip, knee, calf and ankle stay continuous during the shallow supported bend. Both feet remain planted as the body lowers. The quadriceps tint now crosses the shorts without the earlier triangular depth-conflict fragments; the side silhouette preserves the knee and heel relationships.

repairsAndChecks: Uses the native connected ankle, heel, forefoot and toes.
Counter-rotates the toe joint during heel rise and restores the same endpoint pose.
studies.observations: The heel rises and returns while the toes remain part of the same continuous forefoot. Front and oblique views show all five connected toes, including the small lateral toe. The ankle, instep and calf transition smoothly; toe support remains stable through the authored rise.

limitations: This is an illustrative, adapted CC0 character mesh and authored skeletal animation, not a scan, a clinical anatomy model or a medically validated simulation.

The result has natural continuous human topology and textured PBR materials, but it is not a photoreal digital double or a verified likeness of Sydney Sweeney. Hair still uses textured cards rather than individually simulated strands.
Mint patches indicate semantic surface regions, not dissected muscles, quantified activation or simulated tissue mechanics.
Very close inspection can reveal source texture softness, card-based hair structure, garment edge aliasing and shadow-map resolution.
Some free-orbit limb views and mobile arm framing include adjacent head or torso beneath the fixed headline; the requested limb remains visible and controls remain usable.
Playback review samples screenshots across a loop boundary; it is not frame-by-frame inspection of every rendered frame or every possible camera angle.
